name: DICK, the Hon. Dugald (Milton) Milton

headline.note: The documented career consists of political-staff employment, party employment and elected office, all excluded under the codebook. A 2024 interview identifies the Beddall electorate-office position as full-time, but hours and exact transitions elsewhere remain unavailable and no source establishes whether there was any other paid work during university or the 2016 candidacy interval. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: The interview establishes university attendance in1993, not completion that year; unsupported end date removed. Official biography confirms BA, but study endpoints and concurrent paid work remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded from the two employment headlines.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. David Beddall MP
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography supplies the 1993-1998 interval. Dick's 2024 interview describes the offer as a full-time job after he campaigned for Beddall while studying; exact appointment and cessation dates and leave are unavailable.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.employer: Office of Senator the Hon. John Hogg
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography and parliamentary handbook identify the employer, role and year interval. Exact dates, hours and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography separates the 2000-2004 organiser role from the later state-secretary role. Queensland Hansard records that the serving organiser was appointed state secretary in May 2004. Exact start, transition date, hours and leave remain unavailable.
career_spells.counting_note: Party employment is excluded from the two employment headlines.

career_spells.role: Acting State Secretary, later State Secretary and campaign director
career_spells.evidence_note: Hansard13May2004 refers to a media report of11May describing appointment as acting secretary the previous night. It supports May2004, not an unambiguous12May appointment. Later official biography identifies state secretary2004–08. Exact substantive appointment/payroll transition and cessation remain unknown; resignation announcedDecember2007 for effectMarch2008.
career_spells.counting_note: Party employment is excluded from the two employment headlines.

career_spells.role: Councillor for Richlands Ward; Deputy Opposition Leader 2008–12; Opposition Leader 2012–16
career_spells.evidence_note: ECQ records Dick's election on 15 March 2008. The official parliamentary biography separates Deputy Opposition Leader 2008–12 and Opposition Leader 2012–16. In April 2015 he said he would serve his full term through the local election scheduled for March 2016, which ECQ records as 19 March. These leadership positions are part of the elected office, not additional employment spells.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded from the public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.role: Oxley campaign, including intended full-time candidacy after council term
career_spells.evidence_note: April2015 report describes intention to campaign full-time after the March2016 council election. Prior20March–1July derived boundaries were not evidence of actual work dates; retained2016 activity only. Paid status, legal employer, hours and actual endpoints unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Candidate and party activity is excluded; 'full-time candidate' is not converted into a full-time employment finding.

career_spells.role: Member for Oxley; Speaker of the House of Representatives from 26 July 2022
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography records election to Oxley on 2 July 2016 and election as Speaker on 26 July 2022.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded from the employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Report names Dick as co-reviewer with Jane Garrett; publicly reportedJune2014 during council tenure. Commission dates, paid basis and hours unknown. Do not assume2013 in report title is appointment year.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary biographies list the national presidency without dates, hours or paid basis. It is retained as a party office rather than inferred employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Party office is excluded from the public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Current official biography lists delegate service from 2001. No cessation, remuneration or hours are published; this is a party position, not assumed payroll employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Party office is excluded from the public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Current official biography records the 2011–18 interval. No paid basis or hours are stated; it overlaps council elected office and is preserved as a distinct party position without additive duration.
career_spells.counting_note: Party office is excluded from the public/private employment headlines.

research_notes: The frozen parliamentary occupation text compresses all Queensland Labor work into an elected-official span of 2000-2008; the current official biography and handbook separate organiser and state-secretary roles.

No evidence was found of non-political public- or private-sector employment. That absence is not converted into zero because sources do not rule out student/casual work or paid work during the 2016 candidacy interval.

Follow up payroll or personnel records for exact electorate-office and party transitions, hours and leave; establish whether the 2016 full-time candidacy was paid and whether any earlier paid work accompanied university study.
Previous precise2016 candidate boundaries were inferred from elections and have been removed; dates of paid work cannot be established from campaign intentions.

2026-10-02 follow-up: corrected1993 study endpoint, acting-secretary wording and Hansard locator; removed synthetic candidate days; added campaign-review role from original report. Searches for first jobs, UQ graduation and pre1993 work found no verified additional employer or hours. Father giving someone else a butcher job and unrelated US doctor results are not this member. Courier-Mail direct open returned Internal Error; indexed interview passage accessible. Reported full-time Beddall offer retained, but continuous hours/leave across1993–98 not independently established. Council election dates still need comparison with actual legal service/retirement dates; no headline calculation depends on these excluded roles. Follow up UQ dates, personnel/party records and candidacy pay; no outreach undertaken.

2026-10-03 follow-up: current official parliamentary biography completes council leadership coding (Deputy Opposition Leader2008–12, Opposition Leader2012–16) and adds National President of Australian Young Labor plus national-conference delegate from2001 and Queensland state-conference delegate2011–18. These are preserved as distinct political/party positions with paid basis and hours unknown, not treated as public/private employment or additive full-time duration. Fresh searches of UQ, electorate-office, party and interview sources did not identify a pre-1993 employer, degree boundaries, exact payroll transitions or 2016 candidacy pay. Next: personnel/payroll or archived appointment notices and UQ conferral record.
